answer.rationale: Rated by how close each memory's evidence sits to sustainable long-term qualified revenue, and by what it fails to say. memory_57 is strongest (5): it names qualified revenue directly, in established customers, and explicitly checks the main downside risk (retention) — outcome, quality, and durability are all present. memory_44 (4) speaks to pipeline quality in the highest-value segment, which is a good revenue proxy, but stops at pipeline rather than closed or retained revenue, and says nothing about cost-to-serve of sales assistance. memory_31 (3) claims a 'durable' lift, which is a genuine durability signal, but the outcome is first-week activation in SMB with no link to revenue and no guard against simplification inflating low-intent signups. memory_86 (3) reports completion, time-to-value, and early adoption — plausible leading indicators, but three steps removed from revenue, and it omits whether shortened onboarding hurt later depth of use. memory_73 (2) is the most seductive given the competitor's entry pricing, but it is exactly the memory whose omissions matter most: it reports acquisition and revenue lift with no margin, no retention, no cohort durability, and no statement of horizon — discount-led acquisition is the classic case where short-term revenue and sustainable revenue diverge, so it should not be treated as licence to match the competitor on price. memory_91 is weakest (1): week-one engagement and 'first meaningful action' are pure proxy metrics, with no revenue figure, no quality filter, no retention check, and no time horizon; it is the least attached to the objective. Two cross-cutting cautions apply to the whole set: every entry is a one-line consolidation with its source archived, so none can be re-audited for effect size, sample, or confounds; and all predate the competitor's entry, so the SMB-facing findings (31, 73, 86) were measured in a market that no longer exists. The current 6% activation and 4% onboarding declines may be competitive mix shift rather than funnel decay, which further weakens the proxy-metric memories as a basis for this week's single slot.
